Express vectors, dyadics and scalars in a coordinate system

Source: R/vector-operators.R
express.Rd

express(expr, system) re-expresses a vector, dyadic or scalar field in system; with variables = TRUE the base scalars of other systems are substituted too. matrix_to_vector() and matrix_to_dyadic() turn component matrices into vectors and dyadics, orthogonalize() applies Gram-Schmidt, directional_derivative() differentiates a field along a vector, and scalar_potential_difference() evaluates the potential difference of a field between two points.

Usage

express(expr, system, system2 = NULL, variables = FALSE)

matrix_to_vector(matrix, system)

matrix_to_dyadic(matrix, system)

orthogonalize(..., orthonormal = FALSE)

directional_derivative(field, direction_vector)

scalar_potential_difference(field, coord_sys, point1, point2, origin = NULL)

Arguments

expr

A vector, dyadic or scalar expression.

system, system2

Coordinate systems (CoordSys3D()).

variables

Substitute the coordinate variables.

matrix

A 3 by 1 (or 3 by 3) matrix.

...

Vectors.

orthonormal

Normalize the result.

field

A scalar or vector field.

direction_vector

A vector.

coord_sys

A coordinate system.

point1, point2

Points.

origin

For physics reference frames, the origin point used by scalar_potential_difference(); ignored for CoordSys3D systems.

Value

A vector, dyadic, expression or list.

Examples

N <- CoordSys3D("N")
A <- orient_new_axis(N, "A", Symbol("q"), N$k)
express(A$i, N)
#> (cos(q))*N.i + (sin(q))*N.j
matrix_to_vector(Matrix(list(1, 2, 3)), N)
#> N.i + 2*N.j + 3*N.k
orthogonalize(N$i + 2 * N$j, 2 * N$i + 3 * N$j)
#> [[1]]
#> N.i + 2*N.j
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> 2/5*N.i + (-1/5)*N.j
#>
